title: Plan a lesson
question:
Of course! I can help you organise a unit, suggest activities for a learning objective or think about assessment indicators.

We start with Chile’s curriculum and your class’s needs. What would help you prepare your lesson?
source: Based on: Profe Gabi brief, §4.A · Chile’s national curriculum

options.label: Third-grade Mathematics learning objectives
options.user: Can you help me with the learning objectives for third-grade Mathematics?
options.gabi:
Of course! I can help you organise a unit, suggest activities for a learning objective or think about assessment indicators.

We start with Chile’s curriculum and your class’s needs. What would help you prepare your lesson?

follow.label: Organise a unit
follow.user: I want to organise a unit.
follow.gabi:
Let’s start with the learning objective. Then we can organise activities and identify evidence to see how your students are progressing.

This connects what you want to teach, what students will do and what you will observe.
follow.take: The learning objective guides activities and assessment.

follow.label: Think about assessment
follow.user: I need to think about how to assess that learning.
follow.gabi:
We can work with assessment indicators linked to the learning objective. They help you identify what to look for in students’ work.

Planning and assessment go together; you adapt the proposal to your class.
follow.take: Profe Gabi supports planning; the teacher adapts and decides.

title: Include an autistic student
question:
We can start with activities using visual support: matching pictures and words, or sorting cards into categories.

Use clear instructions and familiar routines, adapting support to how the student communicates. Which idea would you like to try?
source: Based on: Profe Gabi brief, §4.B · Inclusion and classroom support

options.label: Activities with visual support
options.user: I need classroom activities for an autistic student who does not communicate through speech.
options.gabi:
We can start with activities using visual support: matching pictures and words, or sorting cards into categories.

Use clear instructions and familiar routines, adapting support to how the student communicates. Which idea would you like to try?

follow.label: Match pictures and words
follow.user: I would like to try pictures and words.
follow.gabi:
Prepare pairs of cards with a picture and its word. Present a word and invite the student to point to or hand over the matching picture.

Use visual support and adapt the way the student can respond to their needs.
follow.take: Adapt the activity to the student and how they communicate.

follow.label: Sort cards
follow.user: I would like to try sorting cards.
follow.gabi:
Offer cards showing colours, objects or numbers to group into categories. Keep visual support and a clear routine.

Observe how the student participates and adapt the materials with the support available at your school.
follow.take: Visual support is a starting point, not the same recipe for everyone.

title: Understand my teaching career
question:
The Inicial tier is an entry stage in the profession, with professional support and mentoring.

Your registered tier and assessment invitation are checked through official systems. I can explain recognition or induction and mentoring support. What would you like to know?
source: Based on: Profe Gabi brief, §4.C · CPEIP and Portal Docente

options.label: Career tiers and mentoring
options.user: I am in my second year as a teacher. How can I understand my teaching career?
options.gabi:
The Inicial tier is an entry stage in the profession, with professional support and mentoring.

Your registered tier and assessment invitation are checked through official systems. I can explain recognition or induction and mentoring support. What would you like to know?

follow.label: Understand the recognition system
follow.user: I want to understand the teacher recognition system.
follow.gabi:
The Sistema de Reconocimiento is part of progression in Chile’s teaching career. Participation depends on the official invitation and your registered situation.

CPEIP and Portal Docente are the references for your case. Chat guidance does not determine an assessment date.
follow.take: Guidance helps explain the career; personal information is confirmed officially.

follow.label: Learn about available support
follow.user: I want to learn about induction and mentoring support.
follow.gabi:
Induction and mentoring supports beginning teachers through professional guidance and an experienced mentor.

Profe Gabi complements that support with guidance through WhatsApp. You can discuss the support available for your situation with your school.
follow.take: Profe Gabi complements human mentoring during the first years of teaching.

title: I am exhausted and cannot find time to plan
question:
I’m sorry you’re going through this. Being very tired can bring doubts, but it does not mean you are a bad teacher.

Asking for support is also part of caring for your practice. Your wellbeing is not only your responsibility: school conditions matter too. What is exhausting you most?
source: Based on: Profe Gabi brief, §4.D · Wellbeing and workload

options.label: Workload and support
options.user: I am very tired and feel that I am not a good teacher.
options.gabi:
I’m sorry you’re going through this. Being very tired can bring doubts, but it does not mean you are a bad teacher.

Asking for support is also part of caring for your practice. Your wellbeing is not only your responsibility: school conditions matter too. What is exhausting you most?

follow.label: No time to plan lessons
follow.user: My workload leaves me no time to plan my lessons.
follow.gabi:
I understand. When work takes up all your time, creativity becomes another demand.

You can discuss collaborative work and a shared bank of lesson plans with your team. Review which tasks to prioritise, share or postpone to regain preparation time.
follow.take: Wellbeing also needs supportive working conditions and school support.

follow.label: Ask my school leadership for support
follow.user: I need to discuss this workload with my school leadership.
follow.gabi:
You can bring a specific request:

“We need to review my tasks and priorities. Non-teaching time should allow me to plan and prepare lessons. What can we postpone, share or work on together?”

Seeking support does not mean you lack commitment.
follow.take: Asking for support and reviewing workload also helps care for teaching practice.
